title: Shard commit window oversubscription causing stale prefix writes and numeric instability
creator: Mina Park
description:
Summary:
A recent kernel-selection optimization that merges small attention shards into a pooled execution window is oversubscribing the commit phase for prefix/KV cache entries when prefill and decode micro-batches interleave. The oversubscription leads to stale prefix writes (older KV slots overwriting newer ones) and intermittent numerical instability in downstream softmax outputs under mixed-precision paths. This manifests as token hallucination/regressions on a subset of customer workloads and a small but measurable increase in perplexity in regression suites.

Reproducibility:
- High-frequency on multi-request scenarios with small per-request context (<128 tokens) and high concurrency (>=16 inflight per-GPU).
- Easier to reproduce with a synthetic workload that alternates short prefill batches and single-step decode calls at ~200 qps.
- Repro command & minimal test harness: linked in comments.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Kernel-selection heuristics merge attention shards from nearby requests into a single fused kernel to improve utilization. The fused kernel assumes a single ordered commit window for prefix writes, but prefill tasks can hand off to decode tasks after a scheduling yield. When the scheduler reorders the micro-batches, the fused commit routine applies KV writes by slot offset rather than absolute sequence id. If two micro-batches target overlapping KV slabs, a late-arriving commit can overwrite a newer slot with older content.
- Mixed-precision accumulation in the fused kernel (FP16 accumulation followed by FP32 accumulation path in fallback code) amplifies small rounding discrepancies. When stale KV entries are read back in, the attention softmax can hit numerically sensitive regions causing token distribution skew.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: medium (some customers observe semantic drift on long-context prompts intermittently).
- Platform: P99 tail latency spikes and increased error counts related to cache-mismatch assertions in a small percentage of serving nodes.

Acceptance criteria for fix:
- Deterministic repro no longer fails under the same synthetic harness at 1M iterations.
- End-to-end regression runs show no increase in perplexity vs baseline and no semantic regression in failing prompt suite.
- New unit/integration tests covering micro-batch reorder with fused kernels land; nightly fuzz test added to catch slot-overwrite scenarios.

Proposed mitigations / plan:
1) Short-term mitigation (hotfix): enforce commit ordering barrier in the kernel dispatch for fused shards where overlapping KV slots are detected. This is a conservative guard that prevents overwrite but reduces some utilization. Deploy to canary (2 nodes) ASAP.
2) Mid-term fix: change fused commit to use absolute sequence IDs for KV slot mapping and add atomic compare-and-swap guards on commit paths where hardware supports it. This requires modifying the kernel metadata layout and the runtime kernel selector.
3) Long-term: revise scheduler heuristics so that micro-batches that will be fused are guaranteed a non-overlapping KV region or are pinned to a per-request commit epoch. Also remove mixed-precision fallbacks that change accumulation order; implement compensated summation in accumulation path to reduce numerical drift.

Rollout/testing:
- Canary on runtime-1.20 with hotfix barrier enabled. Monitor token-level divergence metrics, KV-cache mismatch logs, and tail latency for 72h.
- If stable, progressive rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with staged feature-flag flip.

Risks and trade-offs:
- The hotfix barrier increases latency and reduces GPU utilization on heavy shard-fusion workloads. Risk acceptable short-term for correctness.
- Full fixes require kernel metadata changes which will need coordination with compilation and driver teams; potential for new regressions if sequence-id mapping is incorrect.

Notes and links:
- Repro harness (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro/tree/ENG-324568/shard-commit-harness
- Design doc (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Shard+Commit+Window+Investigation
- Initial PR with barrier hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2134
- Telemetry dashboard (kv-mismatch & token-divergence): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-commit-anomalies

Next steps (owner: Liam):
- [Day 0-1] Validate and record deterministic repro on an isolated node. Add reproducer as unit test.
- [Day 1-3] Land hotfix barrier PR and deploy canary.
- [Day 3-10] Iterate on mid-term kernel metadata patch; prototype atomic commit check.
- [Day 10-20] Integrate compensated accumulation and scheduler changes; expand tests and run full regression.
